title: Guard the Faith as a Wall
english: By this, emperor, the power of your true faith is walled about; keep it inviolable for us. Let no heretic slip under the Church and take away one of the Trinity, leaving what remains dishonored.
translator_notes: Copy-text PG 18 Khazarzar Allocutio ad Constantinum [Sp.]. PD.
True OET; Pass A ≠ Pass B. Melito skipped; never Cyril Matthew densify.
Attributed Eustathius; PG marks Spurious — disclosed in About.
orientation: Eustathius is addressing Emperor Constantine directly, urging him to protect the orthodox faith of the Trinity from heretics.

title: Arius the namesake of madness
english: Arius is the one responsible for this word and this gathering—the namesake of the madness. Somehow, without our knowing how, he was enrolled in the presbytery of the Church of the Alexandrians, and he escaped our notice, though he was a stranger to the teaching of the thrice-blessed prophets and apostles. He is not ashamed to rob the only-begotten Son and Word of the Father of his consubstantiality with the Father, and this worshiper of what is created is eager to number the Creator together with creation.
translator_notes: Copy-text PG 18 Khazarzar Allocutio ad Constantinum [Sp.]. PD.
True OET; Pass A ≠ Pass B. Melito skipped; never Cyril Matthew densify.
Attributed Eustathius; PG marks Spurious — disclosed in About.
orientation: Eustathius is addressing Emperor Constantine and has just urged him to keep the faith walled about and let no heretic dishonor any person of the Trinity; now he names Arius as the source of the present disturbance.

title: Persuade or expel Arius
english: You could persuade him, Emperor, to change his mind and stop opposing the apostolic teachings. Or, if he remains fixed in the impious acts of false teaching in which he has been caught, may you remove him utterly from the Church, the fold of Christ and of us, so that his muddy sophistry may not make prey of simpler souls.
translator_notes: Copy-text PG 18 Khazarzar Allocutio ad Constantinum [Sp.]. PD.
True OET; Pass A ≠ Pass B. Melito skipped; never Cyril Matthew densify.
Attributed Eustathius; PG marks Spurious — disclosed in About.
orientation: Eustathius, having accused Arius of denying the Son's consubstantiality and numbering the Creator with creation, now addresses the emperor directly with a two-part request.
